# FedRAMP GCC-Moderate — Microsoft Purview and Defender: compliance role and residual boundary gap

> **Purpose of this finding.** This is a single classification artifact for
> distribution to the FedRAMP/OIS reviewer and the internal team. It states
> (1) the compliance role Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender play in the
> agency's RMF/FISMA authorization, and (2) the residual capability gap that
> remains when those tools operate inside the FedRAMP GCC-Moderate authorization
> boundary. It does **not** introduce a new telemetry signal — every gap named
> here is already registered in `gcc-moderate-telemetry-gaps.yaml`; this finding
> is the consolidated Purview/Defender view over those existing rows.

## 1. Constraint

Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender are the agency's **payload-protection**
and **detection-and-response** control surfaces. Their positive control-closure
role is documented in the Federal Application-Aware Networking (AAN) series:

| Tool | AAN home (closure corpus) | Controls closed |
|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Purview** (sensitivity labels, DLP, Data Map, Audit, CMK) | Vol III — Data Protection (Purview) | AC-4, AU-10, MP-2–5, SC-12/12(1)/13/17/28, PT-1..7 (with Book 17) |
| **Microsoft Sentinel + Microsoft 365 Defender** (SIEM/XDR, detection engineering) | Vol III — SIEM/XDR Detection | AU-6(×3), AU-7/8/11, SI-4(×4), IR-4/6/8 |
| **Microsoft Defender for Cloud** (CSPM/CNAPP) | Vol III — Cloud-Native Security Posture | CM-6, RA-5, CM-7, SC-7, SI-3, SA-11 |
| **Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management** (MDVM + KEV) | Vol III — Vulnerability Management | RA-5(×3), SI-2(×2), SI-5, CM-7(×2) |

Both tools are **required, not optional**, for a complete FedRAMP Moderate
posture: the network and identity layers regulate the pipe; Purview classifies
and protects the payload; Defender/Sentinel convert the log warehouse into an
active detection engine (AU-6 is not satisfied by a passive archive).

**The constraint:** several of the analytic and real-time signals these tools
expose in Microsoft **commercial** cloud are **unavailable, restricted, or
inferred-blocked** at the GCC-Moderate service level, because FedRAMP Moderate
boundary controls (SI-4, AU-2, AU-3, SC-7) sever the client-side and
Microsoft-hosted-ML telemetry paths those features depend on. The tools remain
authoritative for their *enforcement* function; they are **degraded for their
*analytic* function**. Per the boundary analysis's standing finding, **full
compensation is not achievable** for every degraded signal.

## 2. Evidence

### Primary sources

- **[Microsoft Purview auditing solutions overview — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-solutions-overview)** (accessed 2026-07-09) — Audit Standard 180-day retention; Premium 1 year; 10-year add-on. Drives the retention cliff (FINDING-008).
- **[Microsoft Entra ID Protection — risk detections — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks)** (accessed 2026-07-09) — real-time, ML-driven risk scoring; the Microsoft-hosted signal path is not exposed at the GCC-Moderate boundary.
- **GCC-Moderate telemetry-gap register** — `src/uiao/canon/data/gcc-moderate-telemetry-gaps.yaml` (signal SSOT, extracted from the M365 GCC-Moderate Telemetry & Boundary Assessment External v1.0, 2026-04-25).
- **GCC boundary gap registry** — `src/uiao/canon/gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml`, `GAP-INT-001` (Endpoint Analytics `SILENTLY_BLOCKED`, DiagTrack endpoints blocked by FedRAMP Moderate controls; `COMPENSATED` via `UIAO-TELEM-001`).

### Interpretation authority

In-boundary rebuild verdicts are owned by **B.1.3** (`docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/boundary/B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd`). The verdict taxonomy — `fixes` / `partial-substitute` / `partial-bounded` / `not-fixed` — is B.1.3's, reproduced here per-row.

## 3. Capability gap

### 3.1 Purview — payload protection retained, analytic depth degraded

Enforcement (labels apply, DLP blocks, CMK protects) is **unaffected**. What is
degraded is the *analytic and forensic* layer:

| Gap-matrix row | Signal degraded at GCC-M | B.1.3 verdict | Residual after rebuild |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sensitivity-label-usage-analytics` | Bulk label-change / mass-decrypt analytics | **fixes** | Label history reconstructed from Purview audit |
| `dlp-behavioral-richness` | Override / near-miss / fingerprint context | **fixes** | Pattern rules only; no content-fingerprint model |
| `copilot-ai-prompt-response-telemetry` | AI prompt/response richness | **partial-substitute** | Incident counts only; behavioral patterns unrecoverable |
| `m365-usage-analytics-historical-pivots` (Purview Audit 180-day cliff) | 12+ month forensic pivots | **fixes** (retention) | Requires agency long-retention store / Audit Premium — see FINDING-008 |

### 3.2 Defender / Entra Identity Protection — detection retained, real-time latency degraded

| Gap-matrix row | Signal degraded at GCC-M | B.1.3 verdict | Residual after rebuild |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entra-identity-protection-realtime-risk` | ML impossible-travel / atypical-IP risk scoring | **fixes** | Detection latency minutes→hours; **no global Microsoft threat intelligence** |
| `cae-realtime-revocation-paths` | Sub-second CAE token revocation | **partial-bounded** | Minutes, not sub-second; ZTMM Optimal unreachable |
| `app-protection-policy-violation-analytics` | Real-time app-protection violation flags | **fixes** | Snapshot-driven, not real-time behavioral |

### 3.3 Defender for Endpoint device telemetry — Endpoint Analytics silently blocked

`GAP-INT-001` (feature registry): Endpoint Analytics renders in the portal but
its dashboard is **permanently empty** — DiagTrack endpoints
(`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `vortex.data.microsoft.com`) are blocked by the
Moderate boundary. Status: **COMPENSATED** by `UIAO-TELEM-001` (in-boundary
aggregation via Graph + Defender `DeviceEvents`). Underlying signal rows:

| Gap-matrix row | B.1.3 verdict | Residual |
|---|---|---|
| `device-boot-performance` | **partial-substitute** | Depends on exportable device telemetry |
| `app-reliability-crashcount-hangrate` | **partial-substitute** | Exploit-attempt clusters partially recovered |
| `resource-performance-cpu-memory` | **partial-substitute** | High value — recovers grey-ware / miner / exfil signal |
| `device-performance-anomalies-regression` | **partial-substitute** | Core device-integrity signal partially recovered |

### 3.4 Gap classification summary (for the reviewer)

- **Compensable (fixed in-boundary):** label-usage analytics, DLP behavioral rules, app-protection flags, Identity Protection detection (at higher latency), retention cliff (via storage). Documented compensating controls exist.
- **Partially compensable (residual risk registered):** Copilot telemetry, Endpoint Analytics device signals, CAE revocation latency. Accepted-and-registered residuals.
- **Non-compensable (irreducible):** global Microsoft threat intelligence behind Identity Protection scoring, and commercial sub-second/real-time latency. These are candidate inputs to any future boundary-variance (GCC High) discussion — **out of scope for FedRAMP Moderate**.

## 4. Proposed remedy

### 4.1 Internal (inside substrate scope — load-bearing)

1. Ship Purview unified audit + Defender/Entra sign-in + device events to a
   Sentinel/Log Analytics long-retention archive (single compensating store;
   also resolves FINDING-008's retention cliff).
2. Author agency-side detection content over the exported deltas — the
   Phase 2/3 rules named in B.1.3 (impossible-travel, atypical-IP, mass-decrypt,
   DLP override patterns, elevation anomalies).
3. Keep `UIAO-TELEM-001` active for Endpoint Analytics device signals.
4. Register the residual-risk items (§3.4) in the POA&M with accepted-risk
   dispositions; wire them as continuous drift signals through the Purview /
   Defender conformance-adapter slots (ADR-058) rather than one-shot findings.

### 4.2 External (requires third-party change)

- **None available on the FedRAMP Moderate path.** Real-time latency and
  Microsoft-hosted global threat intelligence are boundary characteristics, not
  licensing gaps. FedRAMP 20x does not address them. Closing the non-compensable
  residuals would require a **boundary-variance decision (GCC High or above)** —
  an OIS/CIO governance matter, deliberately outside this finding's Moderate
  scope.
